age.evidence: Only body weight is given: 'male C57BL/6 mice weighing 25-30 g'. Age is not stated.

sex.evidence: groups of 8 (n =8) male C57BL/6 mice weighing 25-30 g were used. A total of 120 animals were used throughout the study.

psychedelic: Mimosa tenuiflora root-bark alkaloid fraction AF II (containing DMT, bufotenine, yuremamine)

dosing.compound: Mimosa tenuiflora alkaloid fraction AF II (DMT/bufotenine-rich)
dosing.doses_raw: AF II (3, 6, or 9 mg/ kg, s.c.)
dosing.evidence: Mice were treated subcutaneously (s.c.) in the following groups: vehicle (0.9% NaCl) and AF II at doses of 3, 6, and 9 mg/kg ... treated with vehicle or AF II in three groups, at doses of 3, 6 or 9 mg/kg (s.c.). In Experiment 3, 'on days 9 and 10 ... the animals were treated as in the previous section'.

day_night_flipped.evidence: with a light/dark cycle of 12 h each day (7 a. m. and 7 p.m.)

assays.assay_description: AF II (3, 6, 9 mg/kg s.c.) or vehicle was given, followed 30 min later by morphine (10 mg/kg i.p.). Acetic acid (0.6%, 10 mL/kg i.p.) was given 30 min after morphine. Starting 5 min after acetic acid, abdominal writhes were counted for 20 min.

application_type.evidence: Mice were treated subcutaneously (s.c.) in the following groups: vehicle (0.9% NaCl) and AF II at doses of 3, 6, and 9 mg/kg; and intraperitoneally (i.p.) in the morphine group

setup_restrain.evidence: No restraint described during the writhing count; restraint is only implied for injections.

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the observation setup (short standard test).

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the observation setup (short standard test).

time_to_assay.evidence: Thirty minutes after AF II administration, the animals received 10 mg/kg of morphine... The AF II-treated groups received acetic acid (0.6%) i.p. 30 min after morphine administration. Five minutes after acetic acid administration, the number of writhing movements was recorded for 20 min.

sample_size.evidence: For each experiment in this study, groups of 8 (n =8) male C57BL/6 mice ... were used (5 groups: vehicle, morphine, AF II 3/6/9 + morphine).

outcomes.summary: Morphine reduced writhing by ~99% versus vehicle. Pre-treatment with AF II (3, 6, 9 mg/kg) did not interfere with morphine analgesia, with writhing still reduced by ~97% at all doses.
outcomes.statistics: ANOVA followed by Dunnett's post-hoc test: ***p < 0.001 vs vehicle for morphine and all AF II + morphine groups
outcomes.evidence: Preadministration of AF II at doses of 3, 6, and 9 mg/kg did not interfere with the analgesic effect of morphine.

B1_num_measures.evidence: the number of writhing movements was recorded for 20 min

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only a total count is reported (Table 2).

B4_ethological.evidence: A writhe was operationally defined as a contraction of the abdomen followed by stretching of the hind limbs (nociceptive response).

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Writhes counted by blinded observers ('Group 2 was tasked with assessing the animals' behavior').

D1_continuity.evidence: the number of writhing movements was recorded for 20 min

assays.assay_description: Mice received escalating morphine (25–100 mg/kg s.c., twice daily) for 8 days, plus a further 100 mg/kg dose on the morning of day 9. Two hours after the last morphine dose, AF II (3, 6, 9 mg/kg s.c.) or vehicle was given. Naloxone (1 mg/kg s.c.) followed 30 min later. Jumping, paw tremor and walk in reverse were counted for 30 min immediately after naloxone.

application_type.evidence: treated with vehicle or AF II in three groups, at doses of 3, 6 or 9 mg/kg (s.c.)

setup_restrain.evidence: Behavioural observation of jumping, paw tremor and walk in reverse; no restraint described.

food_restriction.evidence: No food described in the observation setup.

water_restriction.evidence: No water described in the observation setup.

time_to_assay.evidence: 30 min after treatment, the animals received an injection of naloxone (1 mg/kg, s.c.)... Immediately after naloxone administration, behavioral observation began for a period of 30 min.

sample_size.evidence: groups of 8 (n =8) male C57BL/6 mice (vehicle, morphine, AF II 3/6/9 mg/kg)

outcomes.summary: Morphine withdrawal increased jumping, paw tremor and walk in reverse versus vehicle. AF II at 3 and 6 mg/kg reduced jumping (by 80% and 55%). Only 9 mg/kg reduced paw tremor (by 91%), and no dose affected walk in reverse.
outcomes.statistics: Morphine vs vehicle: ***p < 0.001 (unpaired t-test). Jumps: AF II 3 mg/kg ***p < 0.001, 6 mg/kg *p < 0.05 vs morphine. Paw tremor: 9 mg/kg ***p < 0.001 vs morphine (one-way ANOVA + Dunnett).
outcomes.evidence: doses of 3 and 6 mg/kg were significant (***p < 0.001 and *p < 0.05, respectively) in reducing the number of jumps by 79.87% and 55.40%... Only the treatment with the 9 mg/kg dose was significant (***p < 0.001) in reducing the paw tremor sign by 91.04%... None of the AF II doses showed a significant reduction in the walk in reverse withdrawal sign.

B1_num_measures.evidence: The effects of AF II on the somatic signs of withdrawal (jumping, paw tremors, and walk in reverse) were recorded.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Only totals over 30 min are reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Somatic manifestations include stereotyped behaviors such as jumping, paw tremors, and walk in reverse.

D1_continuity.evidence: behavioral observation began for a period of 30 min (day 9)

D2_session_duration.evidence: behavioral observation began for a period of 30 min

assays.assay_description: Day 9 of the withdrawal protocol. AF II (3, 6, 9 mg/kg s.c.) or vehicle was followed 30 min later by naloxone. Immediately afterwards, mice were placed in an acrylic box (30×30×15 cm, black floor, 9 virtual squares) for 5 min. Four-paw line crossings and rearing were counted.

application_type.evidence: the animals were treated as in the previous section ... AF II ... 3, 6 or 9 mg/kg (s.c.)

setup_habituation.evidence: Paper only states 'Each animal was placed individually in the middle of the field'; prior apparatus exposure is not addressed.

setup_restrain.evidence: Each animal was placed individually in the middle of the field to count the number of four-legged crossings (a spontaneous locomotor activity)

food_restriction.evidence: Empty acrylic box; no food in the apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Empty acrylic box; no water in the apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: 30 min after treatment, the animals received an injection of naloxone (1 mg/kg, s.c.)... Immediately after naloxone administration, the animals were observed for 5 min in the OFT.

sample_size.evidence: A new experiment involving five groups (n =8/group) was conducted.

outcomes.summary: During withdrawal, AF II at 3 and 6 mg/kg increased crossings (~76–77%) and rearing (~163–195%) versus the morphine group. 9 mg/kg showed reduced activity, which the authors describe as a descriptive inverted-U pattern.
outcomes.statistics: Crossings: *p < 0.05 for 3 and 6 mg/kg vs morphine. Rearing: ***p < 0.001 for 3 and 6 mg/kg vs morphine (ANOVA + Dunnett).
outcomes.evidence: Treatment with AF II at doses of 3 and 6 mg/kg showed a significant result (*p < 0.05) by increasing the number of crossings... Doses of 3 and 6 mg/kg also showed a significant effect (***p < 0.001) by increasing rearing

B1_num_measures.evidence: count the number of four-legged crossings ... and the number of rearing actions

B4_ethological.evidence: the number of rearing actions that did not involve abutting the wall (exploratory act scored distinctly)

E1_environment_type.evidence: acrylic box (transparent walls and black floor, 30 x 30 ×15 cm)

E6_spatial.evidence: divided into nine squares of equal areas (virtual zones)

E7_social_context.evidence: Each animal was placed individually in the middle of the field

D1_continuity.evidence: observed for 5 min in the OFT (day 9)

D3_recording_days.evidence: The open-field test (OFT) was performed on that day [day 9]

assays.assay_description: Day 10 of the withdrawal protocol. Mice were re-treated with AF II (3, 6, 9 mg/kg s.c.) or vehicle, followed 30 min later by naloxone. Mice were then placed in the light compartment of a two-compartment acrylic box (each compartment 27×18×29 cm, joined by a small opening) for 5 min. Latency to leave the light side and time in the light area were measured.

application_type.evidence: on days 9 and 10 ... the animals were treated as in the previous section ... AF II ... (s.c.)

setup_restrain.evidence: Each animal was placed individually in the light compartment.

time_to_assay.evidence: on days 9 and 10 ... 30 min after treatment, the animals received an injection of naloxone ... On day 10, the animals were observed for 5 min in the LDBT.

sample_size.evidence: A new experiment involving five groups (n =8/group) was conducted.

outcomes.summary: Only AF II 9 mg/kg significantly increased latency in the light compartment (by ~174%) versus the morphine group. Time in the light area showed a non-significant dose-related trend. The authors caution that prior OFT and naloxone exposure may confound these results.
outcomes.statistics: Latency: *p < 0.05 for 9 mg/kg vs morphine (ANOVA + Dunnett). Time in light: n.s.
outcomes.evidence: In the light-dark box tes, only the 9 mg/kg dose showed a significant effect (*p < 0.05) by increasing latency (45.16 ± 15.23 s) by 173.69% when compared to the morphine group (16.50 ± 6.75 s)

B1_num_measures.evidence: The parameters were latency in seconds (s) and time spent in the light area in seconds (s).

B4_ethological.evidence: Latency and zone time are spatial measures.

E1_environment_type.evidence: The acrylic device used is divided into two parts, called the light and dark areas

E2_shelter.evidence: The dark compartment (black acrylic, 27 x 18 ×29 cm) is poorly lit.

E6_spatial.evidence: divided into two parts, called the light and dark areas, and connected by a small opening

E7_social_context.evidence: Each animal was placed individually in the light compartment.

E8_food_water.evidence: Standard LDBT apparatus with no food or water described.

D1_continuity.evidence: On day 10, the animals were observed for 5 min in the LDBT.

D2_session_duration.evidence: observed for 5 min in the LDBT

D3_recording_days.evidence: The light-dark box (LDBT) test was conducted on day 10.

D5_followup.evidence: AF II was re-administered on day 10 ~30 min before testing.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified the same four assays (writhing, somatic withdrawal signs, OFT, LDBT). All were retained as distinct behavioural paradigms in which AF II was administered.
Writhing test: corrected gemma4's B1 score (1 measure = 0 points) and D2 score (20 min = 15–60 min = 1 point), following qwen/deepseek4.
Corrected gemma4's B1 scores of 2 for the 2–3-measure category to 1 point (somatic, OFT, LDBT).
OFT B4: followed the qwen/deepseek4 majority (rearing scored as a distinct exploratory act = Yes).
OFT setup_habituation: set to not_reported (deepseek4/gemma4 majority). qwen's 'no' is not supported by an explicit statement in the paper.
Age set to not_reported: the paper gives only body weight (25–30 g) and the rubric forbids inferring age.
Writhing application_type set to s.c. (route of the psychedelic fraction). Morphine and acetic acid were i.p. but are not psychedelics.
Dosing schedule kept as 'acute' (modal) with medium confidence. Note that Experiment 3 animals were re-dosed with AF II on day 10 before the LDBT ('treated as in the previous section').
Somatic n_total set to 40 (5 groups × 8) following the qwen/deepseek4 majority over gemma4's 32.
